main_text.p: lr.stio: Affirmantem partem nos tuemur, cujus funda-icus, Phy- meta suo loco proferemus: Ratio potissima depro-mitur ab experientia, quâ constat in genere multa corpora naturalia invicem transmutari: & in specie de metallis nonnullis id manifestissimum, ut pluri-fulminibus. bus suo loco monstrabimus. Rationes, quæ in con-trariam adferri solent partem, elumbes sunt, & vel principium petunt, vel experientiæ contradicunt. Præcipua ratio est: quod species invicem transmuta-ri nequeant: quæ primum petit principium: Deinde dubiam assumit hypothesin, de specifica metallorum differentia: denique totam evertit naturam. Nam si species in speciem transmutari nequit, nulla dabituriani corp. in natura generatio. Qui excipiunt, per, artem non posse corpora naturalia produci: parum videntur habere cognitam rationem, quâ transmutatio me-tallorum peragitur. Partes in transmutatione principales sunt naturæ, seu agentium & patientium naturalium, ministeriales sunt artis, quæ agentia & patientia naturalia tantum applicat: Sic & Medicus non magister, sed minister est naturæ.

Magia naturalis est exactior quædam & ar-caniot[?] naturæ cognitio ad praxin vulgo admirabilem directa: Versaturque in operibus mirabilibus efficiendis, vel futuris prædicendis: unde distinguitur in thaumaturgicam & divinatricem.

The note at the top of the first paragraph is a placeholder for these fragments, not a full transcription. The left margin continues down to the "est quæ-" line near the bottom. The initial M of "Magia" is a decorative letter. The "IV." is set as a section numeral and is treated as a paragraph, not a heading. The footnote "[illegible, ~20 letters]" is a placeholder for the note reading "{...}" at the foot of the page. The text under the first paragraph ends with "Thau-" as catchword.
